answer: Fingerprints are counted in anchor, so that the distribution is public, and beacon lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. The declaration is a lantern header, so 1475 keys running one model collapse to a single share. That is 34 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
